verdict.line: You lose if you let Jayce freely poke in Cannon stance before level 6; you win by forcing stance-locked melee trades where Counter Strike punishes his commitment.

brief.thesis: Jayce's stance swap controls engagement range — Hammer stance is his melee gap-close/knockback form, Cannon stance is his ranged poke/attack-speed form — while Jax has zero ranged threat and wins only when he forces a stance-locked melee exchange. The 53.4% win rate over 337 games reflects that this is decided by who dictates range, not by either champion's raw damage.

theirWindow.when: Jayce in Cannon stance at range
theirWindow.what: His Cannon Q (Shock Blast) detonates for physical damage on anyone it hits or at max range, and Cannon W (Hyper Charge) gives him maximum attack speed for several attacks. Don't walk into that without minion cover, especially before level 6.

yourWindow.when: Jayce commits to melee with Q
yourWindow.what: The instant he leaps in with Hammer Q (To the Skies!) or starts autoing, pop E (Counter Strike): it dodges incoming basic attacks, then stuns everyone around you on an 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown, giving you a free W (Empower)-boosted follow-up.

start.why: Mitigates the chip damage from Jayce's Cannon-stance Q (Shock Blast) and Hammer-stance W (Lightning Field) that you'll eat every time you have to walk up through his poke range.

boots.why: Jayce's Cannon-stance W (Hyper Charge) and his R-transform first-attack both lean on auto-attack damage; the flat reduction blunts both his poke autos and his all-in.

core.why: The proc damage makes your W (Empower)-enhanced autos and Leap Strikes hit far harder once you actually land a stance-locked trade.
Extra sustain on your short-cooldown abilities lets you out-heal Jayce's poke chip in extended skirmishes once you've closed the range gap.
Survives Jayce's R-transform burst combo (armor/MR shred on the first hit) so you don't get deleted the moment he commits his ultimate.

situational.when: the enemy team adds more burst and you need to sustain through extended fights rather than just survive one
jayce keeps kiting you in cannon stance and you need the slow to stick onto him long enough to force a melee trade
the game goes long and you need the extra utility to close out skirmishes rather than more raw damage

runes.keystoneWhy: The HP scaling and sustain from proc'ing Grasp every time you land a stance-locked trade offsets Jayce's early poke damage (59% win rate, 20.8% pick). Master-tier Jax players instead run Lethal Tempo from Precision for the stacking attack speed that pairs with R's own attack-speed stacking — better suited to a player confident forcing early all-ins rather than sustaining through a longer lane.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the best measured result in this matchup (56.3% over 337 games' sample pool) — Teleport resets you after poke-heavy trades and lets you scale into split-pushing once items come online, while Flash is your answer to dodging a Hammer E (Thundering Blow) knockback mid-engage. Exhaust+Flash is a reasonable alternative if you'd rather have a defensive tool against his all-in.

playing.title: Respect Cannon-stance poke
playing.detail: When Jayce is in Cannon stance, his Q (Shock Blast) detonates for physical damage on hit or at max range, and his W (Hyper Charge) grants him maximum attack speed for several attacks. Don't step into that range without minion cover before level 6.

playing.title: Trade only in Hammer stance
playing.detail: Jayce's Hammer Q (To the Skies!) is a leap that slows, and Hammer E (Thundering Blow) knocks back — wait until he's committed to a leap or an auto string before engaging, since that's when he's actually locked into melee range.

playing.title: Hold Q, don't waste it
playing.detail: Jax's Q (Leap Strike) sits on a long 17/14/11/8/5s cooldown early. If you leap in and he answers with Hammer E (Thundering Blow), you get knocked back and your only gap-closer is down for the rest of the trade.

playing.title: Time E to his engage
playing.detail: Pop E (Counter Strike) the moment Jayce leaps in or starts autoing — it dodges incoming basic attacks, then stuns everyone around you on an 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown, locking him down for your full combo.

playing.title: Stack W before trading
playing.detail: W (Empower) refreshes every 7/6/5/4/3s. Pre-load it before every extended trade so your next Leap Strike or auto carries the bonus damage and hits nearby enemies.

playing.title: Use R to stay in the fight
playing.detail: R (Relentless Assault) gives attack speed per strike with bonus damage every third hit — once you're in melee range, keep attacking rather than disengaging; Jayce's kit punishes you for leaving, not for staying.

playing.title: Scale through items, not an early kill
playing.detail: The matchup's 53.4% win rate over 337 games comes from itemization, not lane dominance. Trinity Force and Sundered Sky let you win extended fights that were only even at levels 1-5, so play for stable trades rather than forcing a premature all-in.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoner spells, and every win-rate/pick-rate figure here are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the stance-timing, cooldown windows, and trade-sequencing reasoning is my own tactical read, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Use Counter Strike [E] when Jayce uses To the Skies! (Q). Be careful of using Leap Strike [Q] as he can simply push you back with Thundering Blow(E).
